candidates.exact_span: EPA proposes a revision to the facility temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L to 449 mg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the operative enforceable TDS limit for compliance comparison is 449 mg/L or the prior 497 mg/L depends on interpreting this as a proposed versus effective limit and on the temporal scope of the 'temporary' limit during Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The proposed TDS permit limit, in accordance with 40 CFR §133.101(f), was based 95th percentile of the most recent three years (i.e., 2018-2020) of City's wastewater treatment plant effluent net TDS data.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of which effluent dataset, percentile method, or regulatory basis governs the limit could change the applicable numeric TDS value or leave limit applicability unresolved for measured results.

candidates.exact_span: The 30-day average mass loading limit is, also, revised to 24,992lbs/day from 27,664 lbs/day based on the proposed 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 449 mg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A different interpretation of whether the revised 24,992 lbs/day mass loading limit is in effect, or whether the prior 27,664 lbs/day limit still applies, would change which numeric limit is used for TDS mass-loading compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: The facility is required to continue maintaining the formulated BMP activities and monitoring its effluent quality and quantity on a regular basis with reporting results monthly.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting 'continue,' 'formulated BMP activities,' 'on a regular basis,' and 'reporting results monthly' could change which monitoring and reporting obligations are deemed applicable in FY2025 (B), and whether absent monthly results reflect required-but-missing evidence versus a documented no-data or not-required state (C).

candidates.exact_span: The facility is designated a major POTW for permitting purposes and must supply the expanded pollutant testing list described in the EPA Application Form 2A.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether major-POTW status and the Form 2A expanded pollutant testing list impose applicable monitoring requirements for specific parameters and periods in FY2025 depends on how this designation is mapped to operative permit conditions.

candidates.exact_span: The City of Farmington WWTP is classified as a "major" discharger with a design flow more than 1.0 MGD.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classification as a major discharger above 1.0 MGD may trigger expanded monitoring obligations; a different interpretation of major/minor status or design flow could change which requirements are treated as applicable.

candidates.exact_span: They completed Part D, "Expanded Effluent Testing Data" of form 2A and submitted to EPA as a part of their April 13, 2021 application.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Part D expanded effluent testing constitutes an ongoing monitoring obligation versus a one-time application submission could change which FY2025 monitoring requirements are deemed required (B) and how missing post-submission results are classified when no ordinary numeric result is available (C).

candidates.exact_span: The submitted data are presented in the Table 1 of Section III.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Table 1 of Section III is treated as the authoritative evidence set for parameters without current FY2025 numeric results could change how missing-evidence cases are classified as documented no-data versus unresolved.
